Hi Sofia — thanks for the logs and the sample. A few quick guesses and requests before the call to speed up repro:

1) Can you confirm whether you’re proxying responses through an ingress (NGINX / Envoy / ALB) that has a response timeout or max buffer size? The 140KB payload size in the log is a clue.
2) Could you paste the exact SDK request (full headers + body)? I’ve attached a small request template (sdk-request-sample.txt) with additional tracing headers we ask customers to add (x-rw-trace-id, x-rw-debug). If you can re-run with those headers that helps.
3) For streaming+tool-calls we’ve seen issues with older JS SDKs where chunked streaming and server-side rerankers interact poorly under certain proxy configs — we recommend upgrading to redwood-js@1.2.3 which includes a streaming backpressure fix.

Short repro steps we’ll try during the deep-dive:
- Reproduce with your sample payload in our staging using your sandbox key (we'll use a copy of your payload).
- Toggle stream=true vs stream=false to confirm whether the problem is streaming-specific.
- If streaming fails, test with 'response_chunk_size' lowered to 8KB as a workaround.

If you can run the attached sdk-request-sample and send the output, we’ll triage faster.

Thanks,
Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofia@eastsidebio.com>, IT Admin <it-admin@eastsidebio.com>

Date: 2026-10-06T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Eastside Bio - Next steps and repro for intermittent 5xx during SDK integration

Hi team — quick follow-up and action items from our deep-dive: 

Root cause (summary):
- Repro confirmed in our staging: combination of streaming tool-calls + server-side reranker produced larger streaming frames that interacted poorly with Eastside's NGINX proxy. The proxy has a default 'proxy_buffer_size' and 'proxy_read_timeout' that caused connection termination for chunked responses >128KB.
- The JS SDK 1.2.0 used by Eastside did not apply the streaming chunk-size workaround we added in 1.2.3, so larger frames were sent without backpressure hints.

Immediate mitigation (apply in priority order):
1) Temporary: switch to non-streaming mode (stream=false) for critical pipelines — this prevents dropped connections while we patch the proxy.
2) Short-term fix on your side: increase NGINX 'proxy_buffer_size' to 64k and 'proxy_read_timeout' to 120s; add 'chunked_transfer_encoding on;'. We attached a small patch diff for reference (proxy-fix-patch.diff).
3) Recommended: upgrade redwood-js to 1.2.3 which contains the streaming backpressure and chunk-size adjustments. We will validate key behavior in our staging with your sandbox key.

Planned follow-ups:
- Marcus will run an internal soak test with streaming+tool-calling+reranker and share the results in RED-1347 by EOD 10/06.
- Dev will do a PR with a repro harness and the minimal SDK test-case (will link in the Jira ticket).
- Neha will coordinate a short runbook email for your SREs that lists the exact proxy knobs (we attached repro-playbook.md).

If you want us to push a brief hotfix to your staging (apply change #2) we can do a short window with your Ops team. Let us know preferred time.

Thanks for the quick collaboration — we'll keep updates in the Jira ticket.

Next steps (who does what):
- Eastside Ops: apply temp proxy settings or set stream=false (ASAP)
- Redwood Dev: validate on 1.2.3; post results on RED-1347 (Marcus / Dev)
- Neha: send a short executive note to Eastside leadership recapping progress (completed)

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
